verdict.rationale: Expensify publishes Integration Server API documentation. It covers credential-based (partnerUserID/partnerUserSecret) and OAuth2 authentication, and lets you programmatically download report data and provision accounts. Evidence on how much of the product the API can drive is thin beyond those examples and an unspecified "much more." Missing for 10: endpoint-level evidence for write actions like creating or approving expenses through the API, and independent or hands-on corroboration of API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: how to programmatically download expense report data for analysis or insertion into your accounting package, provision accounts for new hires, and much more
To act on behalf of individual Expensify users, use the OAuth2 authorization code flow to obtain a short-lived access token.
Credential based `partnerUserID` + `partnerUserSecret` Server-to-server integrations with a single Expensify account
To use the API, you will need to generate API credentials.
